newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen holding off on rate hike for now - sources.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen holding off on rate hike for now - sources.

text.p: Moderate growth and low inflation are allowing the Federal Reserve to hold off on changes to monetary policy for the time being, sources close to the Fed said on Friday.
But the central bank hasn't shelved the option to raise short-term interest rates and could still do so in the coming months, the sources added.
A slowdown from the torrid pace of economic activity seen in the second quarter is giving the Fed room to breathe, ponder and time its next move, the sources noted.

"However, this does not mean the Fed has lowered its vigilance against incipient inflation pressures that historically emerge late in a business cycle or that the Fed has given up on its goal of long-term price stability," one source told Reuters.
Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan "took a gamble" when he bet the economy would slow in the fourth quarter, the source said.

"There is increasing evidence of a significant slowdown in economic activity, while there is no evidence yet of an uptick in inflation," the source said. "However, the next policy move is a question mark at this stage," the source added.
